title: Prove cross-arm output identity before accepting an architecture speedup

source.title: vLLM issue #5313: Speculative decoding with temperature=0 should match non-speculative output
source.claim_scope: The project treats exact greedy agreement as expected behavior; this guard generalizes that requirement without claiming any candidate is correct or fast.

implementation_recipe: Freeze the public semantic contract before timing, including whether identity is exact, tolerance-bounded or property-based.
Run baseline and candidate from identical prompt tokens, parameters, seed, dtype, execution mode and termination policy.
Bind every anchor and edge case to baseline and candidate output digests or to explicit tolerance/property evidence.
Reject performance promotion at the first semantic mismatch and record the earliest divergence plus reopen conditions.
validation_recipe: Repeat each arm to distinguish nondeterminism from stable cross-arm divergence.
For exact contracts compare token IDs or output bytes, not decoded display text alone.
Verify that both arms use the same declared precision, reduction policy and semantic oracle; label a higher-precision control separately instead of treating it as stock-baseline identity.
Locate the first mismatching element and preserve both full-output hashes for diagnosis.
Rerun the fixed-budget performance experiment only after correctness passes on current source.
expected_bottleneck_shifts: A failed candidate leaves performance potential unclaimed and redirects work to the earliest semantic divergence.
After correctness repair, the original performance bottleneck must be remeasured because verification or rollback work may have changed.
failure_modes: Each arm is internally repeatable, so their different outputs are mistakenly called equivalent.
A semantic change is hidden behind aggregate quality metrics even though the public contract requires exact identity.
Only the candidate is recomputed in higher precision and equality to a separately recomputed reference is misreported as identity to the stock low-precision baseline.
Only the first output token is checked while divergence occurs later.
Candidate throughput is published while correctness is marked pending.
scope_limits: Exact identity is mandatory only when the frozen public contract requires it; approximate kernels must instead use explicit numerical tolerances and adversarial cases.
Passing a small prompt suite is discovery evidence, not universal correctness proof.

algorithmic_decomposition.baseline_dependency: A performance claim depends on both semantic admissibility and a measured objective improvement.
algorithmic_decomposition.partition_axis: cross-arm semantic comparison before performance promotion
algorithmic_decomposition.combine_rule: Combine case outcomes with logical AND; any required mismatch makes the candidate inadmissible regardless of speed.
algorithmic_decomposition.finalization: Promote only when all required correctness cases pass and their evidence identities remain valid.
algorithmic_decomposition.work_complexity: Linear in compared output elements until the first mismatch, plus hashing for retained evidence.
algorithmic_decomposition.span_complexity: Correctness screening precedes deeper performance measurement and can fail fast.
algorithmic_decomposition.communication_cost: Stores compact digests and mismatch metadata rather than full traces in the decision record.
invariants: correctness is not inferred from repeatability
a failed exactness gate cannot be overridden by speed
the comparison contract is frozen before measurement

candidate_archetypes.name: hash-bound cross-arm exactness gate
candidate_archetypes.template: Compare baseline and candidate on frozen anchor and edge cases, bind their outputs to evidence, and reject the candidate before promotion when an exact contract differs.
